item.title: Mariah Carey Wins Dismissal As Judge Rejects Brother’s Film-Loss Claim
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Mariah Carey won dismissal of her brother's memoir suit after a judge found gaps in his $1.5 million-plus film-loss claim.
item.content:encoded:
Mariah Carey won dismissal of her brother’s memoir suit after a judge found key gaps in his claims. That includes his claim of more than $1.5 million in lost film work.

Judge Leslie A. Stroth threw out Morgan Carey’s latest complaint. The 11-page decision was filed Monday, October 19. The order was signed October 9. It concerns his claims over her 2020 book, “The Meaning of Mariah Carey.”

Morgan sued in March 2021, saying parts of the book harmed his reputation and cost him work. The latest ruling faults his claims about Mariah’s state of mind. It also finds gaps in his claim of lost film work.

The case falls under New York’s anti-SLAPP law. It protects speech on matters of public interest. Morgan had to meet the “actual malice” test. He had to plead facts showing Mariah knew a statement was false or acted with reckless disregard for the truth.

“Notably, Plaintiff fails to provide any proof that Defendant made such statements with knowledge of their falsity or with reckless disregard for the truth,” Judge Stroth wrote.

The judge also found that claims of ill will toward her brother did not meet that test. Morgan had argued that Mariah put book sales ahead of checking her sources. The court found his claims fell short.

The film dispute gave the judge a second reason to reject parts of his case.

Morgan said he and his wife wrote a script called “Devil’s Hollow.” He claimed a producer in Italy backed a film franchise. The plan called for a movie, a prequel, a sequel and a spinoff series. He said the producer pulled out after learning about the memoir. A deal was still being drafted, in Morgan’s account.

He claimed more than $1.5 million in losses from the canceled project and the wider franchise. But he still hadn’t laid out the deal’s terms or an exact sum for his loss, the judge found.

Judge Stroth wrote: “However, Plaintiff still fails to detail the terms of the agreement and fails to quantify the specific amount of damages suffered beyond the general, ‘in excess of $1.5 million.'”

The order directs court clerks to enter judgment. It also denied Morgan’s bid to lift a pause on discovery as moot.

Mariah’s lawyer, John Rosenberg, told Billboard she welcomed the ruling. He said she views it as a win for authors who speak on matters of public concern.

Morgan’s lawyer, Richard Altman, told the outlet he plans to appeal. He said the decision conflicts with earlier rulings in the case.

item.title: D4vd Murder Trial Faces Major Delays As Rumors Swirl About Missing Millions
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: D4vd's murder case takes another turn as questions about his missing millions, new public defenders and a possible 2027 trial delay intensify.
item.content:encoded:
D4vd may have earned millions from his music career, but the singer accused of murdering teenager Celeste Rivas Hernandez is now relying on taxpayer-funded attorneys as his increasingly complicated criminal case moves toward trial.

And if you thought this situation couldn’t get any more bizarre, consider this: His defense team reportedly has approximately 40 terabytes of evidence to contend with.

That’s a whole lot of information. The singer, nee David Anthony Burke, appeared exhausted during his latest hearing. Correspondent Julia Deng described his puffy eyes, longer hair and unusually tired appearance. He’s stressed.

But the biggest issues seemed to revolve along the lines of money and lawyers. The once-promising musician has parted ways with his private attorneys. Now he’s represented by the Los Angeles County Public Defender’s Office.

According to testimony discussed during the proceedings, D4vd reportedly earned between $10 million and $11.5 million from 2023 through 2025. That. is a lot of money. On top of that, his recording agreement was also estimated to be worth as much as $19 million.

So how does somebody associated with that kind of money suddenly become unable to afford private legal representation? Last year had millions and today, nothing?

An attorney representing Celeste’s family has alleged that assets may have been concealed through corporate entities. They also want to know if the property or money was transferred to the singer’s mother.

However, these are questions. The allegations are disputed and unproven at press time. Some how they determined that D4vd qualified for representation after reviewing his financial circumstances. I do not know what they looked at.

Prosecutors are pushing for first-degree murder, continuous sexual abuse of a child under 14 and unlawful mutilation of human remains. He may end up on death row over these charges.

D4vd has pleaded not guilty.

The next hearing is scheduled for January 11, 2027, but a Law&Crime correspondent suggested the actual trial could be delayed even more because of the extensive evidence and changes in legal representation. I was thinking the trial may still come this year. That is apparently not happening.

Celeste’s fam has a reason for their inquiry on the money. They have a civil lawsuit pending.

Their civil attorney has raised the possibility that another person assisted in the alleged crimes or destruction of evidence. This is only an allegation as well. He acknowledged that the allegation was based on information and belief rather than established proof. I wonder if that person has money?

At any rate, no accomplice has been established.

For now, D4vd remains behind bars, his financial situation is dire and his legal future looks bleak.

And we are left with the rumors!

item.title: Jay-Z Reportedly Chooses Himself For 2027 Super Bowl Halftime Show
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Jay-Z's reported halftime pick revives his 2024 comments about waiting his turn, with a possible reveal tied to his SoFi shows.
item.content:encoded:
Jay-Z reportedly chose himself to headline the 2027 Super Bowl halftime show. The move would put the Roc Nation founder on the stage he helped shape for other stars.

Puck’s Dave Brooks reported October 20 that several sources named Jay-Z as the pick for Super Bowl LXI. His report said Miley Cyrus and Justin Bieber had also been in the running. The NFL and Roc Nation did not respond to Puck’s request for comment.

Neither the NFL nor Roc Nation had named a headliner on their current news pages. Puck said a formal reveal could come this weekend, when Jay-Z plays SoFi Stadium. Roc Nation listed his two shows for October 23 and 24.

Jay-Z’s name had been in the mix for more than a month. AllHipHop covered that prospect on September 18. At the time, a source said he might take the job if no other star was booked.

Jay-Z had not ruled it out. In a January 2024 interview with Entertainment Tonight, he spoke about why he had not picked himself.

“I thought it would be selfish to pick myself too early,” he said. “Maybe one year.”

He made those remarks at the premiere of “The Book of Clarence,” as Usher prepared for that year’s game. By then, Roc Nation had helped bring Rihanna and The Weeknd to halftime. It also worked on the 2022 show led by Dr. Dre. Jay-Z had stayed off the stage himself.

Roc Nation began working with the NFL in 2019 as its live music entertainment strategist. The company won Emmy Awards for its work, including for Bad Bunny’s halftime show this year.

Puck reported that the NFL renewed the deal in 2024 for five more years, at $5 million a year. That would keep Roc Nation tied to the show past next February.

The Los Angeles dates will close his “JAŸ-Z30” run. Those shows are set for the same venue as the Super Bowl, less than four months before the game. A pop-up for his anniversary shows is due to close on October 22.

Super Bowl LXI is set for February 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

item.title: Peter Rosenberg Says He & Ebro Finished HOT 97 Pay Arbitration
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Peter Rosenberg and Ebro Darden backed Mero and Kaz while discussing their pay claims and the studio Ebro paid to build.
item.content:encoded:
Peter Rosenberg said he and Ebro Darden had just finished arbitration over pay they say HOT 97 owed them. He spoke out as his old morning team backed complaints from the station’s current hosts, Mero and Kaz, on Monday.

On their own show, Rosenberg said Laura Stylez had finished her pay case, too. He did not say how the cases had turned out.

“We just finished arbitration,” he said. “Laura finished hers.”

Ebro said he paid to build the trio’s studio with a plan to give HOT 97 free content it could sell ads against. That work helped them launch quickly after their exit. He also said he had offered to help Mero navigate the job.

Ebro said HOT 97 had stopped paying to test songs with listeners while they still worked there.

The dispute follows the end of “Ebro in the Morning” in December 2025. The show began in 2012 and ran for more than a decade on New York radio. Rosenberg had joined HOT 97 in 2007, while Stylez joined in 2013. Days after their last radio show, they were back as “The Ebro, Laura, Rosenberg Show” on YouTube. The daily stream kept the trio intact while giving them a home beyond the FM dial.

Station owner MediaCo had praised the early gains of “Mornings with Mero.” Its February 23 release put HOT 97 third in New York morning drive among adults ages 25 to 54 and 18 to 49. It said the average quarter-hour audience was up 18.5 percent in the older group and 30.7 percent in the younger one from a year before. The figures came from January’s Nielsen ratings and covered weekday broadcasts from 6 A.M. to 10 A.M. The company tied those gains to “Mornings with Mero.”

That January report does not show how the two shows fared in the past three months. Kaz said his show had beaten The Breakfast Club for three months despite having fewer resources.

Barrett Media reported Monday that the company had yet to respond in public to the hosts’ claims. The hosts did not share the terms of the pay cases on Monday’s show.

item.title: Swae Lee Sells Miami Estate For $4.35M After Seeking $5.395M
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Swae Lee sold his Miami estate for $4.35 million, more than $1 million below his asking price for the home with a 15-car garage.
item.content:encoded:
Swae Lee sold his Miami-area estate for $4.35 million. The deal came in more than $1 million below his July asking price.

Mansion Global reported the deal after the seven-bedroom home was listed for $5.395 million in July.

The reported deal was about 19% below that first price. Swae Lee paid $4.25 million for the house in April 2023, the outlet said, citing property records. That put the sale price just $100,000 above what he paid more than three years ago. That spread does not show his net profit, since it leaves out the costs of buying, owning and selling the home.

The home’s agents were Roland Ortiz and Eddy Martinez of ONE Sotheby’s International Realty. A post on their website said the estate went under contract after 47 days on the market.

When AllHipHop covered the listing in July, Swae Lee had described the house as a “great escape from my touring schedule.” He praised its backyard, pool deck and sports courts in a statement about his time there.

Built in 1993, the house had 7,831 square feet of space. It stood at the end of a cul-de-sac, with gates to close off the grounds.

JamesEdition’s listing feature described a five-bedroom main house linked to a two-bedroom guest wing. The main house had five baths, while the guest wing had two. That wing had its own full kitchen and living room.

The garage could hold up to 15 cars. It had climate control, seven bays and automated lifts, making it a key part of the home’s pitch to car collectors.

Inside, the home had an 11-seat theater and a billiards room. The wine cellar could hold 500 bottles. A bar sat with the wine cellar, while broad terraces gave guests more space to spread out.

The 1.22-acre estate also had a pool, tennis court and fully equipped summer kitchen for meals outdoors. Mature palm trees grew on the grounds. The main suite looked onto the gardens and had high ceilings, its own gym and walk-in closets. Its onyx bath had two sinks, a soaking tub and a large shower.

item.title: Salt-N-Pepa Warn Artists About Music Contracts Ahead Of Seattle Honor
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Salt-N-Pepa discussed contracts and control before a Seattle honor, with Spinderella joining their October 22 performance.
item.content:encoded:
Salt-N-Pepa named lack of ownership as a major barrier for women in music in a new interview, urging artists to learn what their contracts give away before they sign.

The duo spoke with Seattle magazine ahead of their October 22 honor at the Museum of Pop Culture.

“You can’t really have creative independence if somebody else ultimately controls the work you created,” the duo’s response read.

Salt-N-Pepa also urged young artists to ask hard questions and seek honest advice. They warned that following too many trends can weaken the identity that gives an act staying power.

That message carries weight given their own fight over recordings such as “Push It” and “Shoop.” The pair sued Universal Music Group in May 2025, seeking to reclaim rights to their catalog. They argued that federal copyright law allowed them to end old grants of rights after 35 years.

Judge Denise Cote dismissed the suit on January 8. Her ruling centered on who had granted the rights under the group’s early contracts.

Their lawyers challenged that decision at a September 22 appeals hearing. The duo argued that their agreements with producer Hurby Azor’s company supported their claim. UMG maintained that Azor’s company, rather than the women, had transferred the rights they sought to reclaim.

After the January dismissal, Salt-N-Pepa pledged to keep fighting for artists’ rights. UMG said it had tried to resolve the dispute privately and remained willing to work toward a resolution.

In the new interview, Salt-N-Pepa also reflected on “Let’s Talk About Sex.” They said the song still helps open discussions about consent, sexual health and control over one’s body. They welcomed younger listeners finding their own connection to the group’s records.

The museum’s event page confirms that Spinderella will join Salt-N-Pepa for their gala performance at Sky Church. The event raises money for exhibitions, youth education, community programs and artifact preservation, according to the museum’s published plans for the fundraiser. Archivist Syreeta Gates serves as this year’s event chair.

MOPOP will honor the group alongside Bruce Lee, Jeremy Scott, Halo and the Wing Luke Museum at its Icons of Pop Culture Gala on October 22 in Seattle.

item.title: K. Michelle Wanted More R&B On Her Country Debut
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: K. Michelle said a late song missed her country debut as she weighed what comes next and adjusted to Nashville's approach.
item.content:encoded:
K. Michelle said a song she badly wanted on her first country album, “Jesus & Whiskey,” missed the cut.

In an Entertainment Focus interview, she recalled trying to add R&B records late in the process. “I threw a fit because they didn’t want me to put those on the new album,” she said. One song she wanted was left off because it came late and was not necessarily a fit.

She praised her label for backing the record, with both sides learning how Nashville works. Throughout the process, the label had seen it as a country album.

The nine-song album came out last week through Real Outlawz Records and BBR Music Group. Sugarland’s Kristian Bush produced it, drawing on ties with the singer that go back more than a decade.

Bush told The Tennessean that the music was played live, with everyone in the same room. He kept it simple to give her voice room to lead. That sound includes steel guitar and Nashville player Justin Schipper’s banjo on “Yodel.”

The singer said she chose Bush for his loyalty to her voice and his willingness to give her room to create. Their work together dates to her “Love & Hip Hop” years.

Bush said her clear point of view mattered to the songs. He noted that women who listen to country often want to hear the thoughts they may not say out loud.

The title track puts faith next to human flaws, arguing that belief does not require a spotless life. K. Michelle wrote it with ERNEST, Jordan Dozzi and Rocky Block. Its themes contrast with the harder-edged “Jack Daniel’s,” another early single.

The debate over her country roots is not new. AllHipHop reported in June 2025 that she corrected a host who said she had not grown up with the genre. She pointed to Memphis and her yodeling scholarship.

She told The Tennessean that fans had heard her honor The Judds and Dolly Parton at her shows. Now she hopes new fans will hear the link with her older R&B records. She pushed back on placing artists in one genre, saying the writer and singer behind both styles had not changed.

She said she is already thinking about the next record.

item.title: Killer Mike Joins High Museum’s 100th Birthday In Atlanta
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Killer Mike attended the High Museum's centennial block party in Atlanta, where Mayor Andre Dickens and the Hawks also appeared.
item.content:encoded:
Killer Mike joined the High Museum of Art’s 100th birthday party in Atlanta on Sunday. The milestone comes with a plan for free museum entry on school trips, a cause that runs through his own ties to art.

FOX 5 Atlanta reported Monday that the rapper, Mayor Andre Dickens and the Atlanta Hawks took part in the Centennial Block Party.

The High’s birthday plans include free entry for Atlanta Public Schools’ K-12 field trips throughout the 2026-27 school year. It says about 4,000 students from the district visit in an average year.

Killer Mike grew up taking such trips. When he joined the High’s board in 2018, he told Artnet News that his public school had brought him there. His school also took students to the Atlanta Symphony Orchestra and the Center for Puppetry Arts.

“I’m a product of the High Museum. I’m a product of Atlanta. I’m a product of the Atlanta public school system,” he said in that interview.

Killer Mike wanted kids from working-class and middle-class homes to have those same ties to art. He also wanted people in music and fine art to spend more time in the same rooms. He hoped more money from the music business would then reach the arts.

He traced that wish to school art classes, where teachers helped him learn to love visual art after he left a music program. He took two art courses a day and later began buying art when he earned enough from music.

He also urged parents with tight budgets to take their kids to museums. He said those trips could be a cheap day out and let them share what they saw.

The High’s centennial plans also describe a shift in who visits. It says visitors of color rose from 15 percent of its crowd to 55 percent since 2015. Its outreach includes free entry and after-hours events.

The plans also include public art partnerships with MARTA and the Atlanta Beltline. Guests can keep taking part in birthday tours and other events on the High’s monthly free days. Its plans list UPS Second Sundays and Access for All days.

item.title: LL Cool J Urges Rappers To Stop Chasing Clicks & Build Real Fans
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: LL Cool J challenged the rush for viral hits and urged artists to give strong songs time to find fans who would stick around.
item.content:encoded:
LL Cool J urged rappers and labels to give songs time to find fans, saying a drive for clicks could cost music its feeling.

In a “7PM in Brooklyn” interview released Friday (October 16), he praised Hip-Hop’s artists and music.

Labels, he said, had come to a point where “data was running the show.”

To explain the risk, LL likened it to judging players by stats. Numbers could miss what happened in a locker room or how players helped each other.

For rappers, that meant taking care with each song. Writing for a caption or a quick click could miss the bond between an artist and a listener.

Patience mattered when good work drew little notice. He acknowledged that hurt, but said a small group of loyal fans could grow with each new song.

LL had tested his own writing while making “The FORCE,” his 2024 album with Q-Tip. Before that team-up, he told The Associated Press that the beats he got were better than the songs he wrote.

His long gap between albums still included time in the studio. A fresh burst of drive pushed him to take the work more seriously. For LL, that meant a return to the basics.

The goal was to feel moved by his words and make something fresh. He had not set out to chase trends or repeat his old work. That focus on the song ran through both interviews.

The same issue shaped how one label boss chose talent. In a 2025 interview, Great Day Records founder Baroline Diaz told Music Business Worldwide she would sign an artist with just 200 followers if she believed in the music.

Diaz favored close work in the studio and steady growth over a viral moment. She also described helping artists prepare for interviews and shape their image before going public. Yet she set monthly goals for streams, followers and subscribers. To her, the fans who stayed would buy tickets and merchandise. She could track those goals while she did the work to build an artist.

For LL, the next step after disappointment stayed simple: “Make another good song.”

item.title: Kandi Burruss Teases “Beyond The Gates” Debut With Bill Hamilton Clash
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Kandi Burruss joins Tabitha Brown for a CBS soap guest spot as Kalista Kilroy, whose arrival puts Bill Hamilton on edge.
item.content:encoded:
Kandi Burruss is stepping into “Beyond the Gates” as Kalista Kilroy, a new guest whose arrival gets an awkward welcome from Bill Hamilton in the CBS soap’s weekly teaser.

The Xscape singer will first appear Thursday, October 22, according to Michael Fairman TV. Tabitha Brown will also guest-star that day as Tia Allen. Both women’s names appeared in the closing credits ahead of their planned guest spots.

The promo places Kalista at the country club with Bill, played by Timon Kyle Durrett. “What the hell are you doing here, Kalista?” he asks. Bill is Dani Dupree’s ex-husband and the father of her daughters, Naomi and Chelsea.

Tia conducts an on-camera interview with Dani, played by Karla Mosley. The episode preview describes a celebration of Dani’s life and career disrupted by a surprise guest who reopens old wounds. Naomi, Chelsea and Andre are left to handle the family fallout.

Kalista appears to take part in the interview and calls Bill an “awful husband,” according to Parade. The preview shows him demanding that the interview stop before Dani walks away from the stage.

Over the weekend, Kandi told fans on Instagram, “I can’t wait for you to meet Kalista!” She added, “We’re about to spice things up!”

She encouraged viewers to catch up with the series and said, “I’m so excited to be a part.” The show’s verified Instagram account welcomed her in the comments.

Kandi joins a show that has already welcomed “Real Housewives” personalities Karen Huger, Gizelle Bryant and Wendy Osefo. Kandi and Tabitha also previously shared a scripted-TV home on Showtime’s Chicago-set drama “The Chi,” where Kandi played the mayor’s wife, Roselyn, and Tabitha portrayed interior designer Octavia.

“Beyond the Gates” centers on the wealthy, multigenerational Dupree family in Fairmont Crest, a gated Maryland community near Washington, D.C. Filmed in Atlanta, the drama premiered February 24, 2025, as the first new network soap since “Passions” in 1999. CBS Studios produces it through its NAACP venture in partnership with P&G Studios.

The hour-long drama, now in its second season, airs weekdays at 2 P.M. Eastern on CBS and streams on Paramount+.
